reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or megawatt consumption for individual Azure data center campuses, including this San Antonio facility. The disclosure policy means this campus cannot be ranked or compared on the basis of computing density or grid load relative to other operators' facilities. Without published specifications, its contribution to AI scaling cannot be quantified from operator data.

The San Antonio region hosts a growing number of Microsoft data centers across Bexar and Medina counties, reflecting the company's continued expansion in Texas. Among 133 mapped facilities statewide, only 18 publish power consumption figures. This campus exists within that landscape but remains unquantified in the published data this site uses to assess grid constraints on AI.

The state context ranks this campus 19th in Texas by published MW, a meaningless ranking since Microsoft publishes no MW figure for it. The ranking reflects only that other operators have disclosed capacity at sites in the state. For readers assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, no published grid demand or compute density is available.
